[Lecture 1: Memory and learning]
Retrieval practice means trying to bring previously learned information to mind without looking at the answer. It strengthens later access to that information.
Spaced practice distributes learning sessions over time. Massed practice groups repetitions into one concentrated session.
Recognition is identifying the correct answer when it is presented among alternatives. Recall is producing the answer without alternatives.
Working memory temporarily holds and manipulates a limited amount of information. Long-term memory stores information over longer periods.
A retrieval cue is a prompt that helps access stored information. A useful cue should identify the target clearly without stating the answer.
Corrective feedback provides the correct answer after a retrieval attempt. It can repair an incorrect response.
Transfer is applying learned knowledge to a new context. An application question can test transfer when it requires using a principle in a new situation.
